hypothesis: a GPU MMU page fault right after alive stalls thread 0 (or the garten), so nothing is serviced afterwards: no wake, no slave-port reply, no event
evidence for: RGX EVENT_STATUS 0x130 = 0x200 in run 77 after alive; bit 9 is upstream MMU_PAGE_FAULT. The firmware routes that bit to a DM4 interrupt task (0xb78 = 0x200, thread 0 INTCTX 0xffff) and its handler clears events (EVENT_CLEAR 0x138 at 0x80009a94), yet it stays set: the handler never ran. Our fault check reads only BANK0 (0x12b0). Orchard's A8 maps a plain zero page at GPU VA 0; we do not (request 18). An access the MMU stalls would also leave the slave port pending (inferred)
evidence against: BANK0 = 0 in every run; alive itself was written fine
predicts (not yet looked at): BANK1 0x12c0 bit 0, or BIF_MMU_STATUS 0x12d0 STALLED (bit 2), or the TEXAS bank 0x1430, set; REQ_STATUS (0x12c8/0x1438) holds the faulting address and requester tag; EVENT_STATUS already 0x200 before the first kick

hypothesis: the garten fence: MTS_GARTEN_WRAPPER_CONFIG (0xb50) holds fence address 0xc0000000 but its upper half (FENCE_DM, FENCE_PC_BASE) was never programmed; nobody writes 0xb50 on J81 (not Apple's host, no store in the decoded firmware), while upstream's host sets it at META wrapper init. A fence through an unprogrammed context or DM could fault (feeds 1) or never complete, and META would wait on it
evidence for: upstream pvr_meta_wrapper_init writes IDLE_CTRL = META, PC_BASE = the firmware context, FENCE_DM = META's BIF DM; 0xb50 reads 0xc0000000 (low word only)
evidence against: Apple's iOS host never writes 0xb50 either, and iOS works
predicts (not yet looked at): 0xb54 (bits 63:32) reads 0 or a reset value; the fault address (if 1) equals 0xc0000000

hypothesis: thread 0 never reached its TXSTAT sleep: it is wedged in the access that faulted (the same root cause as 1, seen from the thread)
evidence for: nothing after alive is visible: no second event, no log, no heap change; the slave port stalls exactly when the firmware first gets past alive
evidence against: the loop's literal 0x80009c14 is posted, so the thread reached the loop entry (fwdis)
predicts (not yet looked at): the fault address names the structure the firmware touches right after alive (its scan of the root, a log or trace buffer, a hardware object)

hypothesis: the MTS-to-META line on the A8X needs a hardware enable no one in software sets (an A8X-specific wrapper or SoC wire), so a presented task (0xb10 = 0x10) is never signalled
evidence for: every software-visible input matches Apple's; Orchard never ran its driver on an A8X (A8X note: 'It has not been run on an A8X with our driver')
evidence against: iOS works with the same host and firmware, so the enable, if any, would be in iBoot/LLB state or the PMGR
predicts (not yet looked at): nothing host-visible; X1 negative plus a zero-page boot negative would leave this

hypothesis: the counted DM0 task needs the MTS SCHEDULE_ENABLE (0xbc8) that only META or hardware can set
evidence for: 0xba8 never counts; 0xbc8 reads 0 and ignores host writes
evidence against: neither the firmware nor Apple's host ever writes 0xbc8, yet iOS works; non-counted kicks (run 80) fail as well

hypothesis: a host step between state 1 and the first kick (a token, a second Fender request, the snoop bit)
evidence against: Apple's bootFirmware does nothing between state 1 and the first command (request 20); Fender +8 KICK_STATUS stays 0 (snoop is for state 0 only)

hypothesis: ring or struct convention mismatch, so the ring scan never sees work
evidence against: the DC ring layout is confirmed in both the host and the firmware (requests 19, 22); the wake comes from the MTS, independent of the scan
